answers.M6-S1: When people badly want something, like being taller, they can be fooled easily and believe tricks that seem too good to be true.
answers.M6-S2: So the narrator won't ask other people about it and find out the seed is fake and Billy is just tricking him out of his money.
answers.M6-S3: The narrator thinks Billy is doing him a kind, special favor, but the reader can tell Billy is probably tricking him into paying for worthless seed.
answers.M6-S4: He is secretly worried about being short after hearing Aunt Janet say so, and he really wants to grow taller than Uncle Alec.
answers.M6-S5: To make the seed sound magical and rare, and to explain why he can't get more, so the narrator won't try getting it himself.
answers.M6-S6: It shows the seed isn't working, but the narrator still trusts Billy and makes excuses, which hints he's been tricked and adds humor.
answers.M6-S7: It explains why the narrator believes Billy's claim; Billy's height seems like proof the magic seed works, making the trick convincing.
answers.M6-S8: That Billy wasn't very well liked; people didn't fully trust him, which hints Billy may not be honest about the seed.
answers.M6-S9: He doesn't want to be short like Uncle Alec. It isn't that he dislikes his uncle; he just wants to grow taller than him.
